keyFindings.description: The sentence that tells an operator what this change needs applied is false for the deployments this repository tells them to build, and it is false in the direction that matters: it says no deployment edit is needed. 'this change raises issue_volume's default from 20Gi to 50Gi — a default every project takes rather than a line of one deployment, so the apply this change needs is the image digest alone, with no deployment edit.' The default reaches only a file that sets nothing: config/kubernetes.go:428 is `block := &Kubernetes{IssueVolume: defaultIssueVolume}`, overridden by any explicit value. This repository's own example writes the line — deploy/kubernetes/daemon/legion.yaml.example:69 is `issue_volume: 50Gi` with the comment '50Gi is the default', and docs/kubernetes.md:1135 shows it written too — so a deployment stood up from either carries its own line, which today says 20Gi, and takes no new default at all. Separately, the size rides in the Sandbox's VolumeClaimTemplates and is evaluated when the Sandbox is created, and an issue's Sandbox outlives its pods, so every issue already running keeps the volume it was created with whatever the configuration says. The consequence is the one this issue exists to stop, arriving quietly: the digest is pinned, the caches move onto a 20Gi volume, nothing prunes /legion/scratch, and the kubelet eviction that used to name the offending container is gone — the same paragraph says so four lines later. This is not the 50Gi number, which is the human's and out of scope; it is whether the mitigation reaches production, and the doc actively tells the operator not to look. One sentence fixes it: a deployment that sets runtime.kubernetes.issue_volume keeps its own value and must raise it before the digest is pinned, and a volume already created for a running issue keeps its size. The operator check belongs beside the pod.env check the architect already ran.

flock is declared on PATH and required at an absolute path, so the declaration does not cover the failure it was added to prevent. The rendered install runs /usr/bin/flock by absolute path (plugins.go:211), while the toolchain row asserts onPath(img, …, 'flock') — presence anywhere on PATH — and the Dockerfile's build-time probe is `flock --version`, also a PATH lookup. An image whose base ships flock somewhere other than /usr/bin passes the apt line, the build probe, the toolchain capability and the probe Sandbox, and then fails every installing launch with the shell's 'not found': the exact fleet-wide outcome the declaration exists to catch, which image.go:245-250 and worker.Dockerfile:478-484 both say in as many words. Latent rather than live, since Debian's util-linux puts it at /usr/bin today, which is also why it is minor. Either assert the absolute path the script uses, or render the script with the path the capability found.

ciShapes: The default check-runs page is 30 and these commits carry 25 to 39; read with per_page=100 and --paginate or required names fall off it.
A push that carries code and handoff together leaves the code commit with no run of its own; the head that merges is the one GitHub judged.

A required workflow can have many runs on one head, because pr-title fires on every pull-request edit; the newest decides, and a run cancelled because a later one superseded it leaves no verdict rather than a red one.

While a pull request is CONFLICTING, GitHub runs no `on: pull_request` workflow for any of its activity, so nothing gets CI until the conflict is cured — which is what the forward merge at f714cec148b6 cured.
The non-required `dispatch` lane has rarely settled on this branch, and envoy-smoke was red at one earlier head on a live envoy-infra listener step this diff cannot reach.
